record.original_question: Let u = (u^1, ..., u^{n+1}) ∈ W^{1,n}(Ω, R^{n+1}) be a weak solution of the H-system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = H(u) J_u, where H: R^{n+1} -> R is bounded and Lipschitz. If exactly k of the coordinate functions of u are known to be bounded for some k in {1, 2, ..., n}, must u be continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with $n \geq 2$, and let $H: \mathbb{R}^{n+1} 	o \mathbb{R}$ be a bounded Lipschitz function. Consider a map $u = (u^1, \ldots, u^{n+1}) \in W^{1,n}(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ that is a weak solution of the H-system
$$-\mathrm{div} igl(|
abla u|^{n-2}
abla u igr) \;=\; H(u)\, J_u\qquad 	ext{in }\Omega,$$
where $J_u: \Omega 	o \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is the (vector-valued) Jacobian whose $i$-th component is the determinant of the $n	imes n$ matrix obtained from the Jacobian matrix $
abla u$ by deleting the $i$-th row, multiplied by $(-1)^{i+1}$, so that $H(u) J_u$ corresponds to the prescribed-mean-curvature nonlinearity. Suppose that for some integer $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, exactly $k$ of the coordinate functions $u^i$ are known to be (locally) bounded in $\Omega$. Must $u$ be continuous in $\Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on H-systems with n-Laplacian establishes that locally bounded weak solutions are Hölder continuous (and C^1 when H is Lipschitz), so the case k = n+1 is settled. For the partial-boundedness regime k ∈ {1,...,n}, no resolution was found; recent works on H-systems in higher dimension treat related regularity questions but do not appear to settle this partial-boundedness problem, which seems to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the H-systems in higher dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Studies regularity of weak solutions to H-systems involving the n-Laplacian, noting that locally bounded weak solutions are locally Hölder continuous and that the higher-dimensional case is significantly more delicate.
status_evidence.claim: Full boundedness implies continuity, but partial-boundedness regularity is not addressed/settled.

status_evidence.title: Regularity for solutions of H-systems and n-harmonic maps with n/2 square integrable derivatives
status_evidence.snippet: Treats regularity of conformally invariant systems including H-systems with critical nonlinearity in higher dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Continues to study regularity under structural assumptions; does not resolve partial-boundedness implication.
